title: Wang Chuqin out of WTT Champions Montpellier with injury
standfirst: The world champion has withdrawn from the singles-only event, which starts on Tuesday, leaving Lin Shidong to lead China's men. Sun Yingsha returns at the head of a six-strong women's squad.
body: Wang Chuqin has pulled out of WTT Champions Montpellier through injury, Chinese media reported on Friday. Korea's An Jae-hyun takes his place in the men's draw for the tournament, which runs from 27 October to 1 November at the Sud de France Arena.

The withdrawal leaves Lin Shidong at the head of a five-man Chinese entry alongside Wen Ruibo, Zhou Qihao, Xiang Peng and Liang Jingkun, according to NetEase. China's women's squad is led by Sun Yingsha and also includes Wang Manyu, Kuai Man, Wang Yidi, Chen Xingtong and Chen Yi, who won the Asian singles title on Sunday.

Montpellier's council coverage on Saturday still listed Wang among the headline names, but Chinese outlets report his withdrawal. The home crowd will focus on Félix and Alexis Lebrun. Félix, the reigning European champion, is ranked second in the world and Alexis eighth. Japan's Sora Matsushima, the world No. 1, returns after reaching last year's final, and Flavien Coton and Thibault Poret add to the French entry.
Wang Manyu arrives as world No. 1 again after regaining top spot in the 12 October rankings, while Wang Yidi defends the women's title. Prithika Pavade and Jia Nan Yuan lead the French women.

WTT Champions events are singles-only and straight knockout, so one defeat ends a player's tournament. Chinese coverage noted that points here also matter for qualification for December's WTT Finals in Hong Kong.

Play runs in two sessions a day, at midday and in the evening local time. The finals are on Sunday 1 November, with sessions at 11:00 and 17:30 in Montpellier, an hour ahead of the UK. This is the third edition of the event in the city.
author: michael
